target.title: fix(agents): mark exec/bash read-only shell calls as replay-safe
target.body: fix(agents): strict-agentic retry blocked after read-only exec/bash inspection turns isReplaySafeToolCall always returned false for exec/bash, blocking strict-agentic retry after turns with only read-only inspection commands like ls, cat, grep, or rg. isMutatingToolCall already uses isPlainReadOnlyShellCommand for the same tools — align replay-safe classification to match. Fixes #101890 ## What Problem This Solves Fixes an issue where GPT-5 agent runs using only read-only shell inspection commands (`exec ls`, `exec cat`, `exec grep`, `exec rg`) would silently produce no output when the model's follow-up turn was reasoning-only or empty. The retry that should recover a visible answer was incorrectly blocked. ## Why This Change Was Made `isReplaySafeToolCall` blanket-returned `false` for all `exec`/`bash` calls, marking them as having potential side effects even when the underlying command was read-only. `isMutatingToolCall` already uses `isPlainReadOnlyShellCommand` to correctly classify the same commands — this fix aligns `isReplaySafeToolCall` to use the same check, so read-only shell calls no longer block retry. ## User Impact GPT-5 (strict-agentic) runs that inspect files or search code via `exec`/`bash` before producing an answer now correctly retry when the model's follow-up turn is empty or reasoning-only, instead of silently terminating with no output. ## Evidence Script simulating the replay-safe classification and retry gate before and after the fix: Focused regression tests added to `src/agents/tool-mutation.test.ts` covering read-only commands (`ls`, `cat`, `grep`, `rg`) now returning `true` and mutating commands (`npm start`, redirects, unsafe `rg` flags) still returning `false`.

target.title: fix(codex): suppress stdout/stderr stream errors in sandbox subprocesses
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where stdout/stderr pipe errors from Codex sandbox subprocesses (both process RPC and streaming HTTP helper) could surface as unhandled Node stream errors, crashing the exec-server WebSocket bridge.

## Why This Change Was Made

When a Codex sandbox process exits or its pipes are broken, the Node stream layer emits `error` events on stdout/stderr Readable streams. Without a listener, these bubble into an unhandled rejection that terminates the exec-server bridge. The sibling `http.ts` streaming helper path had the same gap.

The fix mirrors the same pattern used in `src/agents/sessions/exec.ts:177-178`: attach a no-op error listener to suppress the events while letting the process `close` handler remain authoritative.

## User Impact

Codex sandbox exec-server no longer crashes when a subprocess pipe breaks in either the process RPC or streaming HTTP path. Output collection and close signalling continue to work normally.

## Evidence

**processes.ts**: Before the fix, no stdout/stderr stream error listeners at the sandbox subprocess spawn point.

```diff
 const child = spawn(command, args, { env: execSpec.env, stdio: ["pipe", "pipe", "pipe"] });
 managed.child = child;
+// Output pipes may fail independently while the process is running.
+const ignoreOutputStreamError = () => {};
+child.stdout.on("error", ignoreOutputStreamError);
+child.stderr.on("error", ignoreOutputStreamError);
```

**http.ts**: Same gap in the streaming HTTP subprocess spawn path.

```diff
 const child = spawn(command, args, { env: execSpec.env, stdio: ["pipe", "pipe", "pipe"] });
+
+const ignoreOutputStreamError = () => {};
+child.stdout.on("error", ignoreOutputStreamError);
+child.stderr.on("error", ignoreOutputStreamError);
```

**Runtime proof — real sandbox exec-server run**:

Both paths exercised through a live sandbox exec-server WebSocket JSON-RPC bridge
(`ensureCodexSandboxExecServerEnvironment` + real shell backend). A child process
writing 200 lines to stdout/stderr is terminated mid-output; the bridge survives and
a second process confirms full functionality. The streaming HTTP subprocess also
survives WebSocket closure mid-stream.

```text
$ node --import tsx sandbox-exec-server-proof.mjs

[23:19:07] === OpenClaw Sandbox Exec-Server Pipe Survival Proof ===
[23:19:07] Starting sandbox exec-server with real shell backend...
[agent/embedded] codex sandbox exec-server started
[23:19:07] Sandbox exec-server started
[23:19:07] WebSocket URL: ws://127.0.0.1:54218/openclaw-7a143c2f-...

[23:19:07] --- Test 1: Process RPC bridge pipe survival ---
[23:19:07] WebSocket connected, listening for JSON-RPC notifications
[23:19:07] Spawning sandbox process "pipe-proof-1" (200-line output loop)
[23:19:07] Process started: {"processId":"pipe-proof-1"}
[23:19:07] Killing process "pipe-proof-1" mid-output via process/terminate RPC
[23:19:07] Terminate result: {"running":true}
[23:19:08] Process closed: exitCode=1, outputChunks=13
[23:19:08] ✓ Bridge survived — WebSocket state is OPEN
[23:19:08] Starting second process "pipe-proof-2" ...
[23:19:08] Second process output: "sandbox-bridge-survived"

[23:19:08] --- Test 2: HTTP streaming bridge pipe survival ---
[23:19:08] Sending streaming HTTP request to local echo server
[23:19:09] Closing WebSocket mid-stream to trigger pipe errors
[23:19:09] Connecting new WebSocket to verify bridge is still alive
[23:19:09] New connection established — bridge survived HTTP stream interruption
[23:19:09] HTTP bridge verification output: "sandbox-bridge-survived"

[23:19:09] === PROOF COMPLETE ===
[23:19:09] Both process RPC and HTTP streaming bridges survived pipe errors.
```

The same no-op error listener pattern already exists in `src/agents/sessions/exec.ts:177-178`,
confirming this is the repo-standard approach.

target.body: ## What Problem This Solves Resolves a problem where users connecting to a gateway during iOS onboarding ("Gateway Details", step 2 of 4) could easily miss what was happening. Connection progress and failures were rendered as flat text rows ("Status", "Progress") plus a small footer caption — an error like "Gateway rejected the connection" appeared only as easy-to-overlook fine print, with no visible error state, no retry affordance, and no access to error details. ## Why This Change Was Made The connect step now derives an explicit connection phase (connecting / failed / ready) and renders it as the first, prominent element of the Status section: a spinner with the live target while connecting, the existing `GatewayProblemBanner` (icon, semantic tint, Retry/primary action, Details sheet) for typed `GatewayConnectionProblem` failures — the same treatment the Auth step already uses — and a danger `OpenClawNoticeBanner` with Retry for status-text-only failures. The redundant "Status"/"Progress" rows and the footer caption were removed. No new components; the banner, details sheet, and action handlers already existed at wizard level and are reused. ## User Impact During onboarding, users now clearly see whether the app is connecting, why a connection failed, and can retry or open error details directly on the Gateway Details screen instead of digging the failure reason out of fine print. ## Evidence Manually tested on a real iOS device (home-network onboarding). Before: the rejection only appeared as plain text in the "Status" row and a small caption below the section. After: the Status section leads with a prominent connection-state view (spinner + live detail while connecting, e.g. "Verifying gateway TLS fingerprint…"; error banner with Retry/Details on failure).

target.title: fix(msteams): surface quoted message body in Teams quote replies
target.body:
## Problem When a user quote-replies to the bot's message in a Microsoft Teams 1:1 DM, the bot could not see the quoted message content — it only saw the user's new text. Root cause: Teams delivers the quoted text of a quote-reply inside `

…

` (a truncated snippet), but `extractMSTeamsQuoteInfo` only matched `

…

`. The match failed, `quoteInfo` came back `undefined`, and nothing was surfaced to the agent via `supplemental.quote`. ## Fix **1. Parser (primary):** `extractMSTeamsQuoteInfo` now matches `

` **or** `

` (prefers `copy`, falls back to `preview`), and captures the blockquote `itemid` as the quoted message id. Sender extraction (``) is unchanged. **2. Full text via Graph (enhancement):** the `preview` snippet is Teams-truncated, so when the quoted message id is known we fetch the complete text via the app-only endpoint `GET /chats/{chatId}/messages/{id}` (permitted with the `Chat.Read.All` application permission, unlike the delegated `/me/chats` listing) and use it as the quote body. Scoped to non-channel chats (DM + group) whose Graph chat id is a `19:` id — channel quote context is already covered by the thread-parent path. Wrapped in try/catch; **any failure degrades to the truncated preview from fix 1**, so message handling never breaks. ## Notes / limitations - For 1:1 DMs the Graph chat id is the synthesized `19:{aadObjectId}_{appId}@unq.gbl.spaces` (the fork already computes this for media). This has not been exhaustively verified as accepted by the message-fetch endpoint against every tenant; the graceful fallback ensures correctness regardless. A local `messageId → text` cache (extending `sent-message-cache.ts`) is a robust alternative if the synthesized id proves unreliable. - The delegated `resolveGraphChatId` path is untouched (still used elsewhere). ## Testing - `extensions/msteams/src/inbound.test.ts` — added tests for `preview`-only parsing, `copy`-preferred-over-`preview`, `itemid` capture, and a full real-payload case. - `extensions/msteams/src/graph-thread.test.ts` — added tests for the new `fetchChatMessageText` helper (HTML stripping + path, non-HTML trim, error → undefined, no-body → undefined). - Vitest (msteams): inbound + graph-thread suites pass (58 tests); message-handler suites pass (40 tests). - `pnpm tsgo:extensions` and `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` both pass with no errors. ## Evidence — real behavior **Parser, against the exact Teams quote-reply payload** (redacted): ``` BEFORE (copy-only regex): undefined -> quote dropped AFTER (fixed parser): { sender: "", body: "San Francisco right now ... 54-64 °F (avg…)", id: "1783379480258" } ``` **Live in a real Teams tenant** (1:1 DM; personal names + avatars redacted): The bot now reads back the full quoted message instead of only the new text. ![Bot confirms full visibility of the quoted message](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/velanir-ai-manager/openclaw/8c0179ce251ef02169e6d54532689b88608183e0/extensions/msteams/docs/quote-reply-proof/dm-quote-full-visibility.png) ![Bot answers a question about a specific line of the quoted message](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/velanir-ai-manager/openclaw/8c0179ce251ef02169e6d54532689b88608183e0/extensions/msteams/docs/quote-reply-proof/dm-quote-line-lookup.png) Also deployed live on a production Teams gateway (@openclaw/msteams 2026.6.6): gateway restarted clean (`[msteams] starting provider`) and a real quote-reply surfaces the quoted body to the agent. **Validation:** msteams suites 85 passing (incl. a group-chat gate regression test); `pnpm tsgo:extensions` + `:extensions:test` clean. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

target.title: fix(cli): one-shot agent --local runs never export OTel diagnostics
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where one-shot `openclaw agent --local` runs would export no OTel telemetry at all when `diagnostics.otel.enabled: true` and the `diagnostics-otel` plugin are configured: zero spans, metrics, or logs reached the OTLP collector, while the same turns dispatched through the Gateway exported fine. Gateway-to-embedded fallback runs (gateway timeout or transport failure) silently dropped telemetry the same way, so exactly the runs that bypass the Gateway were invisible in tracing backends.

## Why This Change Was Made

Diagnostics exporters are plugin services and were only ever started inside the Gateway process (`startPluginServices` at gateway startup/reload); embedded CLI runs emit diagnostic events in the CLI process where nothing subscribes. The CLI now starts the `diagnostics-otel` service around embedded agent runs via a scoped, non-activating plugin load that honors the same plugin-enablement config as the Gateway, and flushes on exit: drain the async diagnostic-event queue, then shut the SDK down (force flush), bounded by a 10s timeout so an unreachable collector cannot hang the CLI. `diagnostics-prometheus` intentionally stays Gateway-only — it is a pull-based scrape server that is useless in a short-lived process and would race the Gateway for its port. No new config surface; configs without OTel enabled short-circuit before any plugin load.

## User Impact

Operators running one-shot `openclaw agent --local` turns (and runs that fall back from the Gateway to the embedded agent) now get the same OTel traces, metrics, and logs as Gateway-executed turns, flushed before the process exits. Setups without OTel export enabled are unaffected.

## Evidence

- Live before/after on macOS against a local Arize Phoenix OTLP collector: before, one-shot `--local` runs produced zero spans while Gateway runs exported fine; after, a one-shot run logs `diagnostics-otel: logs exporter enabled (OTLP/Protobuf)` and `openclaw.harness.run`, `openclaw.run`, and `openclaw.model.call` spans (with `gen_ai.*` attributes) arrive in Phoenix seconds after the process exits.

Both files pass (9 + 73 tests) rebased on current `main`.
- `pnpm build` clean with no `[INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]` warnings; `tsgo` core and test lanes clean; oxfmt/oxlint clean on touched files. Validation ran locally via `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` (remote Testbox was unavailable in this environment).
